create.title: Uniform direct one-third envelope for the literal M1 and M2 main blocks
create.statement_tex: Let X>=2 be real, X^(1/4)<=D<=X^(1/2), H_D=floor(DX^(-1/4)), and 1<=L<=H_D. For every literal dyadic M1 or M2 block with the actual Vaaler coefficient, M1 spatial chi_4(d), M2 two-shift chi_4(h) factor, both frequency signs, the exact dyadic denominator profile, and the hard top sampled-BV profile, one has B_i(D,L;X)<<_epsilon X^epsilon min(1+D/L, 1+(LX/D)^(1/2)+D^(3/2)(LX)^(-1/2))<<_epsilon X^(1/3+epsilon). If D/L<=X^(1/3), use the frequency-first bound. If D/L>=X^(1/3), then (LX/D)^(1/2)<=X^(1/3) and D^(3/2)(LX)^(-1/2)=D(D/(LX))^(1/2)<=X^(1/4), since D/L<=D<=X^(1/2). Summing the dyadic frequency blocks gives M_1(D;X),M_2(D;X)<<_epsilon X^(1/3+epsilon) uniformly in every active D. This is a weaker fallback than the M9 target exponent 1/4.
create.next_action: Use this only as the unconditional fallback envelope. The one-quarter M1 and M2 hard-core estimates remain the proof target.

create.title: The accepted direct block menu has exact minimax exponent one third
create.statement_tex: On Omega={(delta,ell):1/4<=delta<=1/2, 0<=ell<=delta-1/4}, minimize blockwise among T2S exponent delta-ell, the full second-derivative maximum of (1+ell-delta)/2, (3delta-1-ell)/2, and 0, the trivial exponent delta, and the audited TTY exponent [89(1+ell)+819delta]/1282 with its companion. The supremum of this minimum is exactly 1/3. At (delta,ell)=(1/2,1/6), the entries are 1/3, max(1/3,1/6,0), 1/2, and 770/1923>1/3. Hence this menu proves no uniform exponent below 1/3. This is menu optimality, not a lower bound for the actual sums.
create.next_action: Any exponent below one third requires a new signed estimate on the residual M1 or M2 core, not another selection among the accepted direct rows.

create.title: Unconditional Gauss circle error bound at exponent one third
create.statement_tex: For every epsilon>0 and every real X>=2, P(X)=N(sqrt(X))-pi X satisfies P(X)<<_epsilon X^(1/3+epsilon). The exact H1-H3 identity and H4 Vaaler approximation split the denominator range into an O(X^(1/4)) bottom remainder, pointwise Fejer residuals O_epsilon(X^(1/4+epsilon)), and literal M1/M2 main blocks. M9-direct-one-third-envelope bounds each main block by O_epsilon(X^(1/3+epsilon)); the O(log^2 X) denominator-frequency assembly is absorbed into X^epsilon. The hard top profile, exact products, floors, integer sawtooth jump, both M2 shifts, both signs, and real-X uniformity are retained. This theorem is strictly weaker than GC-target and does not prove M9-M1, M9-M2, or M9 at exponent 1/4.
create.next_action: Keep this as the unconditional fallback theorem while continuing the separate one-quarter M1 and M2 hard-core program.

update.statement_tex: Let X>=2 be real, X^(1/4)<=D<=X^(1/2), H_D asymp D X^(-1/4), and let w_D be an actual active denominator profile, including the hard top truncation. Vaaler's positive Fejer residual satisfies, pointwise in X, (1/H_D)sum_(d asymp D)|w_D(d)|K_(H_D)(X/d)<<_epsilon X^(1/4+epsilon). The two shifted legs have the same bound after the exact grouping n=d(4m-rho), rho in {1,3}. Exact products receive weight one, the floor-compatible integer jump is exact, half-open shells and the top cutoff only restrict the positive majorant, and the far tail is D H_D^(-2) asymp X^(1/2)/D<=X^(1/4). This is a divisor-product proof, not a mean-square argument.
update.reason_for_promotion: Round 91 independently rederives and hostilely certifies the pointwise positive-Fejer product-count proof from H4, the exact profile, and the elementary divisor bound, removing the former circular documentary dependency.
update.next_action: Reuse the pointwise residual theorem directly; do not replace it with a mean-square Fourier argument.

update.statement_tex: For every real X>=2, every active D with H_D asymp D X^(-1/4), and every actual active denominator profile including the hard top, all first and shifted Fejer residual blocks are O_epsilon(X^(1/4+epsilon)) pointwise. The statement includes exact products, both shifts rho=1,3, half-open shells, height floors, the integer sawtooth convention, and dyadic assembly.
update.reason_for_promotion: H4 is source-audited, and Round 91 closes every pointwise product-count, exact-product, shifted-leg, floor, hard-top, and real-X reconciliation seam.
update.next_action: Treat all Vaaler Fejer residuals as proved pointwise; the remaining one-quarter problem lies in the main M1 and M2 sums.

The original reciprocal-block T2S and weighted second-derivative estimates include the hard top sampled-BV profile, so the transformed endpoint cones are not used in the one-third proof.
R5 is proved pointwise by positivity and exact divisor-product grouping; a mean-square Fourier calculation would be the wrong norm.
